Go's app-server dispatches thread start/resume/read synchronously in Router.Handle, has no RequestSerializationQueues equivalent, no running-thread listener command queue, and no thread/rollback RPC/waiters (the deprecated Rust API was later removed in #44915). Synchronous return already keeps the RPC active through its work, so there is no delegated request-lifetime or queued-request cleanup path to port. go build ./appserver green.

commits.subject: Add opt-in registered package execution to the Windows sandbox (#45550)
evidence: Rust #45550 makes the Windows sandbox able to run against a service-registered Core package instead of always materializing a copied helper. Helper resolution is now runtime-aware: `ResolveExeForRuntime` and the elevated `resolveHelperForRuntime` return the source executable directly in registered mode without copying it or creating `.sandbox-bin`, and never fall back to PATH; legacy mode keeps the previous copy-and-materialize behavior. `GatherReadRootsForRuntime`, `GatherFullReadRootsForRuntime`, `GatherHelperReadRootsForRuntime`, and `BuildPayloadRootsForRuntime` thread the runtime through setup, with registered helper roots returning nil and creating no bin directory while explicit bin read roots are preserved. `setup_windows.go` serializes the runtime into the elevation payload (omitted when legacy), rejects helper-owned provisioning in registered mode via `requireLegacySetupRuntime`, and derives the setup user from the process token (`OpenProcessToken`/`GetTokenUser`/`LookupAccountSid`) before falling back to environment names. `setup_main` validates the payload runtime, refuses Full/Provision work for registered Core with `registered Core requires service-owned provisioning`, still allows RefreshOnly and ReadACLsOnly, and skips locking the sandbox bin directory. `identity.go` additionally requires `registeredSetupIsReady()` for `SandboxSetupIsComplete` in registered mode, which is satisfied only by a real OS package identity on the current process. `appserver/windows_sandbox_runtime.go` and `runtime_router.go` now distinguish an explicit caller-supplied cwd from the fallback cwd: when the request omits cwd the Windows sandbox setup start sends no workspace roots instead of granting the server directory. Metrics: `elevated/runner_metrics.go` adds `codex.windows_sandbox.runner_result` with `runtime`/`phase`/`outcome` labels and `success`/`nonzero_exit`/`transport_error` outcomes; `RetryRunnerSpawnOnce` records a startup result and `unified_exec/live_windows.go` records the command result for elevated sessions. Known gap, deliberately not faked: Go has no `windows-sandbox-service` installation record, execution alias, staged runner image verification, background coalesced registration refresh, or service-side proxy reconciliation, so registered mode is validated only locally (app-contained runner plus OS package identity). Readiness is still synchronous rather than Rust's background refresh. Tests: `sandbox/windowssandbox/setup_runtime_like_rust_test.go` (parent runtime selection incl. case-variant env scrubbing, registered mode not materializing helpers, legacy materializing them, registered helper roots creating no directory, explicit bin read root preserved), `elevated/runner_pipe_test.go` (registered runtime uses the app-contained runner), `elevated/runner_metrics_test.go`, `bin/setup_main/win/setup_runtime_like_rust_windows_test.go`, `setup_ownership_like_rust_windows_test.go`, and `appserver/runtime_router_test.go` (`TestRuntimeRouterWindowsSandboxSetupStartWithoutCWDHasNoWorkspaceRootsLikeRust`). commits.subject: Disable V8 optimization paths affected by array sort bugs (#45760)
evidence: Rust #45760 sets --no-maglev --no-turbolev --no-turbo-inline-array-builtins during code-mode V8 initialization because the pinned V8 can inline Array.prototype.sort with incompatible element kinds when a comparator mutates the receiver, allowing an object to be stored in an integer-elements array, and adds an integration test that requests top-tier and Maglev optimization and inspects element kinds via native syntax. Go has no V8: code-mode cells execute through codemode.NewSobekEngine (github.com/grafana/sobek, a pure-Go ECMAScript engine, see codemode/sobek_engine.go), and a repository-wide search finds no deno_core/rusty_v8 binding, no v8:: API use and no maglev/turbolev flags, so there is no optimizer tier to disable and no element-kind representation that the miscompile could corrupt. The mitigation itself is therefore not applicable. What does carry over is the observable behaviour Rust also asserts, so codemode/array_sort_like_rust_test.go runs a cell that sorts [1,2] and [{},{}] 100 times with a comparator that fills the receiver, then sorts [object,{}] the same way and fails if the original element is still in place; the cell finishes by emitting JSON.stringify([3,1,2].sort((a,b)=>a-b)) and the test asserts the single text item is [1,2,3]. Verified with go test ./codemode -count=1.

Structural note: Go has no connected-channel replay-only runtime outside the closed agent-thread carrier and no postponed-turn input queue, so those Rust internals map to the retained composer/queue state. commits.subject: Keep the TUI responsive during clipboard copies (#47847)

PRIMARY publications coalesce to the latest and flush before busy is released, while middle-click reads use request IDs and are invalidated by new key input so stale reads cannot paste. commits.subject: Fix thread unloading after disconnect during MCP startup (#50380)
evidence: Rust #50380 keeps the thread listener alive when the requesting connection closed during required MCP startup, so idle unloading still reclaims the thread while the request result stays ConnectionClosed. Go's listener equivalent is the retained-thread idle lifecycle. Round 970 records closed transports in RuntimeRouter.closedConnections (guarded by clientInfoMu, cleared by a successful initialize) from ConnectionClosed, and markResponseThreadLoaded no longer re-subscribes a connection that closed while required MCP startup was still running: it arms scheduleThreadIdleUnload instead, so a thread cannot stay loaded with a dead subscriber. unloadIdleChildThread now broadcasts thread/closed after the eviction, matching Rust's ThreadClosed on idle unload. Tests: TestThreadStartFinishingAfterConnectionCloseStillUnloadsLikeRust (disconnect before publish, then no subscriber, idle unload, empty thread/loaded/list and thread/closed), TestThreadStartWithLiveConnectionSubscribesThenUnloadsLikeRust, TestInitializeReopensClosedConnectionLikeRust. Verified with go test ./appserver -run 'Idle|ThreadLifecycle|ThreadLoad|ThreadStart|ConnectionClosed|WorkspaceSwitch|AccountSession|ThreadClosed' -count=1; full go test ./appserver still fails only on the pre-existing Rust-checkout protocol/manifest drift and RuntimeRouter analytics timeouts, reproduced without this change. Residual: idleThreadEvictable deliberately admits only persistent non-subagent children, so Go keeps root and ephemeral-root threads resident and the Rust ephemeral thread/start unload-by-idle scenario has no Go counterpart; the fix covers every thread Go can evict.

commits.subject: Avoid sharing violations when repairing Windows runtime ACLs (#51822)
evidence: Round 735 (implementation): runtime ACL repair never opens a target with MAXIMUM_ALLOWED. acl_windows.openACLHandle requests READ_CONTROL for DACL reads and READ_CONTROL|WRITE_DAC only for an actual update, so repairing an active node.exe held open with FILE_SHARE_READ no longer fails with a sharing violation (verified on Windows: MAXIMUM_ALLOWED conflicts with that share mode, READ_CONTROL|WRITE_DAC does not). Root-only grants also keep a null DACL instead of replacing it, and ensureRuntimeTreeReadable revalidates only after a changed DACL so intentional deny ACEs do not fail the repair, matching Rust ensure_allow_mask_aces_with_inheritance_impl/ensure_runtime_tree_readable. Regression: TestEnsureRuntimeTreeRepairsHeldRuntimeFileAndPreservesDenies holds node.exe with FILE_SHARE_READ across two repairs, then checks read/execute access, no write/DELETE/WRITE_DAC grant, and surviving read/write deny ACEs. Tests: go test ./sandbox/windowssandbox/... -count=1; go build ./...

commits.subject: Fix idle cleanup for disconnected multi-agent v2 children (#52081)
evidence: Rust #52081 starts lifecycle listeners for persisted multi-agent v2 children even with no initialized clients, defers attachment until an earlier runtime cleanup finishes, keeps ephemeral children loaded, and raised the default unload delay to 30 minutes. Go implements the listener as the retained-thread idle lifecycle: ThreadManager.SetThreadRetainedHook arms scheduleThreadIdleUnload when a persisted child becomes live, so a child created after the client disconnects still unloads (TestIdleChildCreatedWithoutClientDisconnectsLikeRust); turn admission pins residency and awaitPendingThreadUnload makes a resume/turn start wait for or reject against an in-flight eviction (TestIdleLifecycleWaitsForPendingCleanupLikeRust); ephemeral children and roots stay resident (TestIdleLifecycleKeepsEphemeralAndRootThreadsLikeRust), while the per-thread zero-delay override still evicts an ephemeral non-subagent (TestIdleEphemeralThreadWithZeroOverrideUnloadsLikeRust, TestIdleEphemeralSubagentStaysLoadedEvenWithZeroOverrideLikeRust); queued mail survives eviction (TestIdleUnloadPreservesQueuedMailLikeRust). The 30-minute default this commit introduced was superseded by Rust #57242 back to one minute, which config.ThreadUnloadDelaySecs already matches (config/thread_unload_delay_like_rust_test.go). Round 970 additionally records closed transports so a start that outlives its connection cannot pin a dead subscriber (#50380). Verified with go test ./appserver -run 'TestIdle|TestThreadUnloadDelay' -count=1.

commits.subject: Check daemon feature overrides and prompt for mismatch recovery (#55442)
evidence: Implemented: app/daemon_compatibility.go ports Rust compatibility_warning (#55442/#47318). Explicit -c/--enable/--disable toggles merge into one CLI layer (a features table replaces earlier dotted keys), removed features are skipped, legacyManagedConfigTomlFromFile/Mdm layers and configRequirements featureRequirements override the launch flags, and experimentalFeature/list decides the rest (removed stage is inert, an unreported feature counts as disabled). An optional attachment downgrades only non-restartable issues to the Running without the shared background server warning; everything else is a CompatibilityError with the Rust reason text and FAILURE_HINT.

Implemented: app/daemon_recovery.go plus tui/onboarding/daemon_recovery.go port daemon_recovery::check. The blocking pre-TUI menu offers run without daemon / restart with these settings / cancel, preselects Cancel, caps the settings preview at three rows plus and N more, offers restart only for a managed daemon (LifecycleVersion reports a backend) with restartable features, persists the confirmed shared settings through LifecycleRunner.RestartWithFeatures, and re-checks compatibility exactly once. A missing terminal is fatal and cancel/esc returns the CompatibilityError.

Automatic startup now calls StartWithFeatures(nil) (Rust start_with_features(&Default::default())), so the daemon keeps its saved settings until a confirmed recovery restart; daemonStartupWarning reports the compatibility warning ahead of the auto-start exclusion warning.

Fixed features.FeatureEntry to decode the Rust name wire field (the JSON round trip previously dropped every catalog key), which the compatibility check and the /experimental popup need to read a real server catalog.

Tests: go test ./app -run TestDaemonCompatibility|TestDaemonFeatureMismatches|TestReadDaemonCompatibility|TestResolveDaemonCompatibility|TestDaemonAutoStart -count=1; go test ./tui/onboarding -run DaemonRecovery -count=1; go test ./features -count=1; go test ./tui/... ./appserverdaemon -count=1; go build ./...

evidence: network/proxy_auth.go owns the CONNECT handshake and retries 407 with Proxy-Authorization; a failed CONNECT is reported as ProxyConnectError with net/http's 'Proxy Authentication Required' text, while a 407 from the origin over an established tunnel stays an ordinary response.
network/proxy_auth_windows.go uses SSPI Negotiate/NTLM (github.com/alexbrainman/sspi) with SPN HTTP/<proxy host>, matching Rust's libcurl gssnegotiate+ntlm behavior without cgo.

network/proxy_auth_transport.go keeps one http.Transport per (proxy,target) route and exposes BaseTransport/ReplaceBaseTransport/WithoutSystemProxy so policy wrappers, custom dialers and custom CA roots survive the wrapper.
Wired into NewHTTPClient(respect_system_proxy=true), the remote TUI WebSocket dial, and the remote plugin HTTP pool; Rust's libcurl named-pipe bridge is N/A because Go owns the CONNECT socket.

commits.subject: Avoid retaining unneeded output items in HTTP response streams (#57563)
evidence: Go's stream mapper has no inference-trace attempt or WebSocket last-response sender layer: `responsesStreamAccumulator` holds only the completed items its AgentResponse returns to the turn, so there is no tracing/continuation copy to gate. The remaining duplicate payload was the accumulated tool-argument buffer: the accumulator kept every `function_call_arguments.delta` / `custom_tool_call_input.delta` string in `functionCallArgDeltas`/`customToolInputDeltas` after the completed item already carried it. `releaseToolInputDeltas` now deletes those buffers at `response.output_item.done` and at terminal response output, releasing a completed item's payload while the response stream is still open. Test: go test ./model -run 'ResponsesStreamAccumulatorReleasesCompletedToolInputDeltas' -count=1
